steps.body: Multiplying a whole number by 10 makes each digit worth ten times as much: 7 ones become 7 tens, or 70.
steps.narration: Multiplying a whole number by 10 makes each digit worth ten times as much: 7 ones become 7 tens, or 70.

widget.prompt: Build an array with 10 rows of 4.
widget.factorFeedback: That rectangle covers 40 squares, but not as 10 rows of 4. Build the arrangement the fact describes.
widget.lowFeedback: That is fewer than 40 squares. Keep building until the array is complete.
widget.highFeedback: That is more than 40 squares. The array should stop at 10 rows of 4.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents ten-times facts.
invariants: The manipulated model and the mathematical relationship for ten-times facts must stay consistent.
misconceptions: Changing a visible feature without preserving the relationship that defines ten-times facts.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: What change would make the model stop representing the same mathematical relationship?

explanationVariants: 10 × 7 = 70 — one of the table facts worth knowing on sight.

commonErrors.feedback: That is 10 short of the product — one whole group of 10 is missing.
That adds the two factors instead of multiplying them. 10 × 7 means 10 groups of 7.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Skip-count by 7, 10 times — or lean on a fact you already know and adjust.
